summary: The comment said both ids are caller- or device-influenced; command_id is server-minted. Harmless (log_token applied as defence in depth). Also found by docs-writer. Fixed in 1144f7ceff (comment reworded).

The new line carries command_id and agent_id but not the request cid (the A4 correlation id in audit rows and response bodies). Audit rows never carry command_id, so a caller's cid reaches the line by agent_id and time only. Found independently by architect, sre and security-guardian, echoed by consistency-auditor, compliance-officer and enterprise-readiness. Needs cid passed into the store overload or logged by both callers: a signature change on both surfaces, not cheap. The comment now states the limit (1144f7ceff). Accepted NICE residual, no issue filed; revisit if operators report the join is a problem.
kShuttingDown was logged at warn; five server sites log shutdown-time cancellations at info. Fixed in 1144f7ceff: shutting_down logs at info, the other three at warn.

kStoreDegraded is logged but was not asserted through the store overload (the existing store_degraded tests use the seam overload). Derived LOW (bounded blast radius), native SHOULD. Fixed in 1144f7ceff: a non-PG test drives it with a pool whose connection is refused.

The test swapped the default logger by hand and never dropped its registry entry, so a logger whose sink writes to a destroyed ostringstream outlived the test (latent: no flush_all in the tree; an ASan scratch repro crashes on apply_all(flush)). Found by cpp-safety (who claimed the borrowed-data policy floor; derived LOW, native BLOCKING), cpp-expert, quality-engineer, unhappy-path. The floor claim was not adjudicated: fixed in 1144f7ceff by moving to LogCapture, which drops the entry, so the question is moot.

CHECK(captured.str().empty()) for the answered read accepted no output at all, so an unrelated store log line would fail it (a false red), and no assertion pinned the level. Fixed in 1144f7ceff: the test counts the marker lines (3) and asserts the level word.

No operator doc or changelog sentence named the new log line (not one of the six required doc items; optional). Also raised by enterprise-readiness. Fixed in 1144f7ceff: one sentence in the changelog fragment.

A stalled stderr or file sink blocks the synchronous default logger's sink mutexes, so a poll worker blocked in the new warn line keeps its kLiveRead lease and the drain's own log lines block too. This commit's increment is one line per no-answer read (at most 4 per 20 s): I8, LOW. The class itself (every spdlog call in the server shares the sink mutexes) derives I5/E5 MEDIUM and is pre-existing, not introduced here. Nearest tracked relative is the agent-side #5049. Accepted: not this commit's to fix; raise as its own sre item if wanted.

Timeout, incomplete, shutting_down and store_degraded answers write no outcome audit row (MCP writes requested and a success row only; REST writes requested and pre-dispatch failure rows). Countability is held by the requested row, so this is forensic completeness, not a countability gap. Not caused by this commit, which adds the log line as a partial mitigation. Same class as the accepted UP-13 residual.
